items.title: Right question for a bearish market: Not ‘will it fall’, but ‘is the business falling’? 5 large-caps with upside potential of up to 29%
items.description: The best large companies are the ones FPIs own the most. So, when they decide to sell, it is precisely these high-quality stocks that see the heaviest selling. That is one of the reasons why large-cap stocks have been under pressure of late.

items.title: FPI selling crosses Rs 52,000 crore in October as Nifty defies foreign exodus
items.description: Foreign portfolio investors pulled out over Rs 52,000 crore from Indian equities in October, surpassing September outflows. Despite persistent FPI selling driven by rising US Treasury yields and elevated crude oil prices, benchmark indices Nifty and Sensex rebounded sharply, supported by robust domestic institutional buying and IT sector gains.

items.title: FPIs pull out Rs 52,100 cr from equities in Oct so far amid global headwinds
items.description: Foreign portfolio investors have withdrawn Rs 52,100 crore from Indian equities as of October this year. This follows a net withdrawal of Rs 35,861 crore in September, indicating ongoing financial retreat. Elevated crude oil prices, higher US bond yields, and a stronger dollar have affected investor sentiment. Despite temporary buying by foreign investors on October 16, selling in certain sectors continues.

items.title: 10 penny stocks plunge up to 75% in six months
items.description: Over the past six months, 10 penny stocks have corrected sharply, falling between 50% and 75%. The stocks were identified through a screen of companies with a market capitalisation below Rs 1,000 crore, a share price below Rs 20, and a minimum recent trading volume of 5 lakh shares. The screen highlights low-priced, relatively liquid penny stocks that have experienced significant declines during the period. (Data Source: ACE Equity).

items.title: FMCG stocks lost their tag of defensive stocks, will they get it back? 7 FMCG stocks with an upside potential of up to 32%
items.description: Those who have been following the market for long know this: When there is nervousness on the street, money instinctively moves towards a particular sector. That is the one with companies that sell soaps, biscuits, tea – all the everyday things that people buy whether the news is good or bad. Yes, we are talking about the FMCG sector.

items.title: Mcap of nine of top-10 most valued firms surges by Rs 3.65 lakh cr; TCS shines
items.description: Nine of the top ten most valued firms saw a substantial increase in market valuation last week. The BSE Sensex surged over two thousand points while the Nifty experienced significant growth. TCS, Bharti Airtel, and Infosys led the gains alongside other major firms like Reliance Industries and HDFC Bank. In contrast, Larsen & Toubro was the only firm to report a decline in market valuation.

items.title: Bonus issues, stock splits & dividends: HDB Financial, IRFC, TechM among 19 stocks turning ex-record date this week
items.description: Around 19 companies including LTIMindtree, Tech Mahindra, IRFC, HDB Financial Services, and Angel One have fixed their record dates for dividends, stock splits, and bonus issues during the week of October 19-23. Investors must hold shares in their demat accounts by the record date to qualify.

items.title: Can Nifty, Sensex rally further or will bears reign in? 5 factors to steer market this week
items.description: Sensex and Nifty extended gains for a second straight session on Friday, led by IT stocks, which rose for a fourth consecutive session, along with buying in auto, metal and PSU banking stocks. Nifty’s recovery could continue as long as it holds above the crucial 22,750–22,800 support zone.

items.title: DIIs increase stake in 8 midcap stocks in Q2FY27
items.description: Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) raising their holdings in a company can signal growing confidence in its prospects. Based on shareholding disclosures available so far for the September 2026 quarter, we have identified nine NSE midcap stocks that recorded an increase of over 200 basis points in DII shareholding on a quarter-on-quarter basis in Q2FY27, according to StockEdge’s shareholding scan.
